Order follows the book's pages: volume (pp. 441-445), composite solids (pp. 446-447), then surface area (exercises on p. 450 and the summary on p. 457). Ex13-7:10, 11, 12 and 20a are used only as evidence.

reconciled.notes: Mapping: A1/B1, A2/B2 and A3/B3 are the same three objectives. B3's ground (circle, cone, cylinder or prism) is folded into the third objective alongside A3's all-dimensions wording. WE20 (radius of a cylinder multiplied by k) is cited by A2 and B3, so it needed a single home. I put it with the second objective because it scales one dimension (the radius) and derives the k^2 volume factor, which the third objective then applies. The second objective is marked agreed, but A2 is broader than B2: it covers cylinders as well as prisms. Ex13-7:18 (A3 evidence) is an end-of-chapter item, so it is not listed as an exercise item, and it is left out of the evidence because it scales one dimension and does not fit the all-dimensions objective.
